transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me for this curriculum approval meeting. As you know, we're preparing a six-week digital reading-intervention pilot for our sixth-grade students across three middle schools. The intervention block meets three times each week, and we have two programs that have both completed our instructional-evidence review: NorthStar at $18 per student and Trail at $20 per student. Before I finalize the plan, I'd like to hear from both of you. Could the literacy coach please report any instructional requirements or considerations we should be aware of, and could the privacy liaison please share any data-governance requirements we need to address? I want to make sure we've covered all bases before I approve the program, implementation schedule, and data controls.

Yesterday I received the signed privacy addendum for Program Trail, which requires that student-data sharing be disabled and that all pilot data be deleted within exactly 30 days after the pilot ends. transcript.text: Dr. Ellis, I need to flag a critical instructional-fidelity issue I discovered this week. The finalized implementation guide for NorthStar requires five student sessions per week to meet fidelity, which simply cannot fit within our three-session intervention block. Program Trail's approved implementation design, on the other hand, requires exactly three sessions per week — a perfect match for our schedule. I completed this comparison this week, but the procurement summary still lists only the prices and has not been updated with this scheduling information. Based on instructional fit alone, NorthStar cannot be implemented with fidelity under our current structure, and Trail is the only viable option.
